case_title: Sunil Damodar Gaikwad v. State of Maharashtra
accused_occupation: Tailor, employed in a cloth shop
accused_socioeconomic_status: Poor; the Court accepted economic and psychic compulsions arising from abject poverty
accused_victim_relationship: Spouse (wife, killed); father of the two sons (killed) and the daughter (injured)
evidence_type: Eyewitness (daughter PW1 and aunt PW4); medical (autopsy by PW3, FSL blood group match); recovery of scissors and clothing; accused's statement to police (Exh. 29)
confession: Statement to police (Exh. 29) admitting the killings, recorded by PW7 and signed by the accused; the Court referred to it and relied on it for the accused's intent and change of heart
aggravating_circumstances: Killing of wife and two sons while asleep with scissors; multiple stab injuries to daughter and attempted suffocation with a pillow; door bolted from outside leaving injured child. Sessions Court and High Court held the case rarest of rare
mitigating_circumstances: Economic and psychic compulsions; abject poverty; son's asthma requiring constant medication; no prior criminal record; reform possible; not a danger to society; change of heart when daughter questioned him; went to police station
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under ss.302 and 307 IPC; death sentence under s.302; life imprisonment under s.307
high_court_outcome: Confirmed death sentence on reference; dismissed the appellant's appeal, confirming conviction and s.307 sentence
offence_finally_established: IPC s.302 (murder of wife and two sons); IPC s.307 (attempt to murder daughter)
neutral_facts: In the early hours of the morning on 8 July 2008, while members of a household were asleep in two rooms of a family dwelling, the accused allegedly attacked family members with the separated parts of a pair of sharp scissors. The accused's spouse and two sons were stabbed multiple times and died at the scene. The accused also stabbed the victim, the accused's daughter, multiple times. When the victim asked why she was being hurt, she was told that the whole family had to go and the accused would follow. The accused then gave her water, held her on his lap, and pressed a pillow over her mouth, but she did not die. The accused left her in that condition, bolted the outer door from outside, and went to a police station to report the incident. A neighbouring relative heard the victim calling for help, opened the door and found the deceased lying in pools of blood. The victim was taken to hospital and treated. The post-mortem examination recorded death from haemorrhagic shock with haemothorax due to multiple stab injuries, and the doctor opined that the injuries could have been caused by the scissors. Blood on the accused's clothing matched the blood group of the accused's deceased spouse. The scissors and clothing were recovered on the accused's disclosure, and blood-soaked material was collected from the spot. The accused's statement to the police, recorded at the station, described the killings and gave a reason for them. The investigation included an inquest, a spot panchnama and photographs.
offence_severity: Death or imprisonment for life for murder (s.302); the penalty for s.307 is not stated
physical_harm: Death of wife and two sons from multiple stab injuries; daughter suffered multiple stab injuries to chest, abdomen and hands and was pressed with a pillow, but survived
premeditation_planning: Premeditation not expressly found. The Court accepted that the accused intended to wipe out the whole family, and that his intent changed only after his daughter questioned him
motive: Economic and psychic compulsions from abject poverty, the family's income being insufficient, and stress over his son's asthma treatment
key_evidence_accepted: Testimony of the daughter (PW1); aunt's testimony (PW4) on the scene and the victim's statement; medical evidence (PW3); FSL blood group match; recovery of scissors; accused's police statement
witness_credibility: Daughter (PW1) was clear and consistent during investigation and trial; aunt (PW4) corroborated the victim's account; the Court held the evidence established beyond doubt that the accused alone was involved
post_offence_conduct: Bolted the door from outside, went to the police station, and gave a statement admitting the killings
trial_duration: offence: 08.07.2008; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 23.09.2010; Supreme Court: 10.09.2013
legal_representation: Accused: Ramesh Chandra Mishra and Dr. Meera Agarwal. State (Respondent): Sushil Karanjkar and Asha Gopalan Nair
investigation_status: FIR registered on the accused's statement; inquest, spot panchnama, recoveries and photographs done; nine prosecution witnesses examined; trial concluded in Sessions Court
appeal_history: Trial court (Sessions): convicted under ss.302 and 307; death under s.302, life under s.307. High Court: death sentence confirmed; appeal dismissed. Supreme Court: conviction upheld; s.302 commuted to life; s.307 reduced to 7 years RI
prosecution_argument: Not stated. The judgment does not record the State's submissions in the Supreme Court; the lower courts held the case rarest of rare
defence_argument: Main contention was commutation of the death sentence; the appellant also contended he was not involved in the incident
legal_principle_applied: Life imprisonment is the rule and death the exception (s.354(3) Cr.PC); rarest of rare test with crime and criminal tests; balance sheet of aggravating and mitigating factors; socio-economic compulsions as mitigating factors; judicial comity
precedent_relied_upon: Bachan Singh (1980) 2 SCC 684; Machhi Singh (1983) 3 SCC 470; Shankar Kisanrao Khade (2013) 5 SCC 546; Dalbir Singh AIR 1979 SC 1384; Ediga Anamma (1974) 4 SCC 443; Sushil Kumar (2009) 10 SCC 434; Gopal Vinayak Godse AIR 1961 SC 600
sentencing_rationale: The case does not fall under the rarest of rare category; the individually inconclusive and cumulatively marginal facts tend towards life imprisonment, which was held to be till the end of the biological life. The s.307 sentence was reduced to 7 years
judicial_mitigating_factors: Economic and psychic compulsions; possibility of reform and rehabilitation; no prior criminal record; not likely to be a menace or danger to society; the accused intended to kill the family out of abject poverty and changed his intent on being questioned by his daughter
other_sentence_order: If the life sentence is remitted or commuted to a specified period (not less than fourteen years under s.433A Cr.PC), the s.307 sentence of 7 years shall commence thereafter
